messages:
margo: Heads-up — dedicated rollout blocked. Canary on pool-phi shows ~2–3x tail latency for text-gen models after last merge (r1234). SLA risk, holding rollout.
raj: Which metric? p95/p99 or throughput? any customer impact yet?
sasha: p50 ~unchanged, p95 from ~320ms -> 850ms, p99 from 420ms -> ~1s+. Throughput slightly down when seq len >512.
perf-ci-bot: CI perf job job/infra/perf/2026-03-... failed: regression detected vs baseline (p99 +210%). Link: https://ci.internal/perf/5493
oliver: I started a quick bisect. Candidate change is commit abcdef1 (kernel selector + new batching heuristic). It landed in r1234.
raj: Any profiling? flamegraphs / kv cache stats?
sasha: Profile snapshot from canary node attached (condensed):
```
pprof top:
 - matmul_kernel_v2 45%  <-- new kernel
 - batching_router 22%
 - kv_cache_lookup 8% (misses up)
 - other 25%
```
Cache stats around same time: hit_rate 68% (baseline ~92%). Miss rate correlates with increased token-level compute.
oliver: The new kernel (matmul_kernel_v2) appears slower for long sequences on Ampere when combined with the continuous-batching change. On small batches it's fine, but for canary traffic distribution we see larger batches/per-step overhead.
margo: Did the canary config use the new batching heuristic?
oliver: Yes, canary used `batching_policy=auto-v2`. Reverting to `auto-v1` brings p99 closer to baseline in local repro.
perf-ci-bot: Bisect result: guilty=abcdef1, suspected range r1228..r1236.
raj: Is there a quick mitigation we can ship without a full revert? e.g., force kernel selection to v1 via runtime flag?
sasha: We can gate the kernel selector with env `REDWOOD_KERNEL_MODE=compat` and force `batching_policy=auto-v1`. Verified in staging — p99 drops to ~360ms.
cs-ops: We're seeing a support ticket from enterprise-corp reporting slow responses on their Dedicated cluster. Customer is on the rollout path — flagging them and pausing further capacity increases.
oncall-bot: @oncall please acknowledge incident INC-2026-107 (Dedicated canary perf regression).
margo: Decision: hold rollout and apply hotfix toggles in canary clusters, notify CS & affected customers, and open a revert PR for r1234.
oliver: Opening revert PR now: https://git.internal/r/revert-r1234 (WIP). I'll also add an opt-out flag for the new kernel in runtime config.
raj: We'll need a post-mortem. Capture perf numbers, bisect steps, and root cause (kernel interaction with batching + KV eviction pattern).
sasha: Quick note — KV miss spike suggests the batching change altered request interleaving, invalidating some prefix cache locality. Need deeper KV access trace.
margo: Thanks. Action items: 1) oliver toggles kernel+batching in canary (in progress). 2) oliver opens revert PR. 3) sasha collects extended KV traces. 4) raj drafts incident doc and notifies customers.
cs-ops: Acknowledged. I'll update enterprise-corp with a brief status and ETA once we have the revert PR. :thumbsup:
margo: Keep updates short here. Post any CI links or perf artifacts.
perf-ci-bot: CI alert: perf job retriggered against revert branch (pending).
oliver: Revert PR created and queued for review. Rolling back r1234 should unblock dedicated rollout once merged.
margo: Good. Escalate to product if rollback affects feature parity for any customers.
raj: Noted. I'll sync with product.
sasha: Adding one more datapoint — kv eviction threshold change in abcdef1 was subtle (LRU window reduced). Combined with different batching we see a working set thrash. Fix might be small if we tune eviction/window, but revert is safer short-term.
margo: End of thread for now — will reopen if status changes.
